title: TTL cleanup drops unresolved futures without completing waiters
reasoning: cleanup_old_results and clear_all remove stored asyncio.Future objects while leaving the Future instances pending. Any coroutine that already received and is awaiting one of those futures will never be resumed with a result, cancellation, or timeout signal from this storage layer. That turns cleanup/session shutdown into a possible permanent wait rather than a bounded failure path.
reproduction: Create a result future with create_result_future('r1'), let its timestamp expire, call cleanup_old_results(0), then await the previously returned future; it remains pending because remove_result_future only pops it from the dict and never cancels or sets an exception.
recommendation: Before removing futures during TTL cleanup, request-specific cleanup, or clear_all, complete them deterministically, preferably by setting a timeout/cleanup exception or cancelling them if that is the established caller contract. Apply the same behavior to bundle futures.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for cleanup_old_results, clear_all, or waiter behavior after cleanup.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an async storage test that creates individual and bundle futures, runs cleanup_old_results or clear_all, and asserts the returned Future objects are done with the expected cancellation/exception instead of remaining pending.
minimumFixScope: Update ToolResultStorage future removal/cleanup paths and add focused async tests for individual and bundle futures.
